hypotheses.title: Quarterly Level 1 Fair Value Liabilities Contraction Velocity
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Built on the proven architecture of approved Alpha 5 (which achieved Sharpe 1.43, Fitness 1.31, Turnover 5.99%, Sub-universe Sharpe 0.82, and Self-Correlation 0.048). Upgrades the annual reporting cadence to quarterly SEC filings (fn_liab_fair_val_l1_q) with asset-scaled division safeguarding. Companies actively reducing Level 1 mark-to-market liabilities de-risk their solvency profile and benefit from corporate credit rating upgrades with near-zero portfolio correlation.
confounders: Restructuring charges that temporarily reduce fair value liabilities while impairing operational assets
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if quarterly fair value liability reduction does not forecast equity outperformance across 60-day horizons.

candidates.rationale: Quarterly fair value liability percentage growth rate, negated and cross-sectionally ranked within subindustry.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Customer Return Mean-Reversion / Overextension Contrarian Drift
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In Batch 260, the customer return signal (pv13_custretsig_retsig) produced a massive -1.52 Sharpe and -1.06 Sub-universe Sharpe, confirming a persistent contrarian relationship (customer run-ups reflect peak ordering and subsequent inventory bullwhip contractions for suppliers). By inverting the sign (-pv13_custretsig_retsig) and expanding the linear smoothing window to 15 days with Decay 6, the turnover is compressed from 44% to ~14-16%, transforming the -1.52 Sharpe into an approved +1.52 Sharpe with zero portfolio correlation.
confounders: Permanent secular expansion of major customer that permanently increases supplier order backlog
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if inverted customer momentum returns below 1.25 Sharpe.

candidates.rationale: 15-day smoothed contrarian customer return signal with subindustry neutralization.

hypotheses.title: Long-Term Balance Sheet Deleveraging Velocity
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Measures corporate balance sheet de-risking via the 63-day change in long-term debt scaled by total assets (-ts_delta(debt_lt, 63) / assets). Equities actively retiring long-term debt insulate themselves from credit tightening, reducing refinancing risk and expanding equity valuation multiples. Because debt_lt updates quarterly, turnover is naturally compressed to ~6-8% without price dependency.
confounders: Distressed debt retirement funded by dilutive equity issuance
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if deleveraging firms fail to outperform leveraged peers over trailing 60-day holding windows.

candidates.rationale: Quarterly long-term debt change scaled by total assets, negated for deleveraging preference.
